Understanding Your Child's Difficulties

Thank you for coming in and sharing what you have been noticing. You have described several months of worry, poor sleep, limited eye contact, tantrums and attention-seeking in your three-year-old. These are real observations, and they deserve attention.

What we know so far: the parenting questionnaire score of 6 is a screening result, not a diagnosis. It does not tell us your child has a specific disorder, nor does it confirm harm. It simply flags that further conversation and assessment are worthwhile.

We do not yet know the cause. Anxiety, sleep disruption and behavioural changes in a young child can have many explanations, including developmental differences, emotional stress or a combination of factors. No single cause can be identified from today's information alone.

What you can try now: when tantrums occur, staying calm and consistent helps more than yelling or physical discipline. Offering predictable routines, brief positive attention for calm behaviour and simple choices can reduce escalation over time. These are supportive strategies, not a guaranteed fix.

A practical next step is to arrange a structured developmental and behavioural assessment with a paediatrician or child psychologist. This would include direct observation of your child, input from both parents and possibly nursery or childcare settings. It can help clarify whether developmental, emotional or environmental factors are contributing.

Please return for follow-up so we can review what the assessment finds and plan together.
